# Independent audit of the retained-cap cone and power-moment theorem

Audited source: `candidate c8365ce16304e154`, Sections 1–4. The compact-facet predecessor `candidate 449b4d02d42ead2a` and the exact geometric exhaustion in Section 7 of `candidate e70b63e0e6efe01c` were also read.

**Result: PASS.** No correction or missing geometric hypothesis was identified. The theorem is ordinary convex geometry, restricted to the stated closed pointed actual projected cone and an interior approach vector. It does not establish a mixed-depth statement.

## 1. Power optimization

An actual inner ball about the mark bounds the power objective below by a positive constant times the parameter norm to the power p. Strict convexity follows on a common neighborhood of the mark where both compared affine functions are positive. Thus attainment and uniqueness hold even if the optimizer's affine function is negative on part of F. Differentiation is legitimate for every real p>1 because the scalar positive-part power is C1 and F is compact.

The stationarity equation and the pointwise identity h^p=(1+a·(z−x))h^(p−1) give both mass and barycenter identities. Hölder gives the asserted minimum-L^(p/(p−1)) characterization, with the correct exponent −(p−1) on the minimum in the formula for B. The first inequality in this argument can be strict for a competing density on the negative-affine set; the proposed optimizer vanishes there and attains both inequalities. Equality in Hölder gives uniqueness. The point-face convention is consistent.

## 2. Infinite product and all constants

Finiteness of the hinge requires its negative normal coefficient in the interior dual cone. A negative value on a cone ray gives positive linear growth; a null ray on the dual boundary translates a small ball about the marked normal point indefinitely without changing the positive hinge. This produces infinite integral on a positive tangential neighborhood, not merely on a null ray.

The cone sublevel volume is J_Q(b)t^k/k!. Integrating this volume in the height gives J_Q(b)A_+^(k+1)/(k+1)!, including the factorial normalization. The independent scalar scale derivative is

    d/dβ log[(1+β)^(k+1)/β^k]=(β−k)/(β(1+β)).

Consequently β=k uniquely minimizes it and the coefficient is exactly

    A_k=(k+1)^k/(k!k^k).

The tangential parameter is (k+1)a_(k+1); the normal parameter is k n_v. The positive set is an affine cap of the actual product. Its definition correctly omits points where the affine right side is negative rather than adding a spurious bottom face with positive-dimensional volume.

For the normal centroid, radial disintegration with t=n_v·q has exponential radial density proportional to t^(k−1)e^(−t), of mean k. Since the full exponential mean is k v, the unit-slice mean is v. Uniform measure truncated at t≤R instead has radial mean kR/(k+1). Substitution R=(k+1)h/k gives conditional normal mean h v. The two power moments from Section 1 therefore give normal mean v after tangential integration. This also independently verifies the cap's exact total mass and marginal h^k/B.

The bounded cap indicator is feasible for the physical dominated-mass problem. For any feasible density with finite first moments, the affine hinge inequality bounds its mass by the same value. Equality forces density one on the positive affine region and zero on the negative region, up to the null cutting plane. This proves physical optimality and uniqueness without invoking an unbounded-body duality theorem.

## 3. Passage from actual compact bodies

The dependency supplies a fixed full-dimensional ball about the dilated source, almost-everywhere local product convergence, and the global containment K_δ⊂D×Q. It applies to the actual cone, not merely its closure. These are precisely the inputs used here.

The source ball gives uniform coercivity of each actual hinge objective. A fixed strictly dual normal hinge has a uniformly bounded positive region, giving a uniform upper objective bound. Hence actual minimizing parameters have compact closure. Along every convergent subsequence, Fatou applies to the nonnegative hinge times the actual body indicator. The ray argument excludes all non-interior dual limits. The limiting objective is therefore at least the product minimum.

Conversely the fixed product minimizer has a positive region in a bounded normal range over D. Local body convergence and elementary dominated convergence give the matching upper bound. This proves the energy-of-the-cap limit without interchanging an infimum and an integral. Uniqueness of the product parameter then forces convergence of every choice of actual minimizing parameters; uniqueness of each compact body's parameter is unnecessary.

Interior dual convergence bounds all actual retained caps in a common compact normal range. The cutting affine functions converge, and the limiting cutting plane and convex boundaries have zero ambient volume. This proves indicator L1 convergence and first-moment convergence. Dividing by the positive limiting mass gives the asserted probability and tangential marginal limits. No escort-density estimate is being substituted for the physical density ceiling.

## 4. Comparison and exact calibrations

Dividing the already-audited energy coefficient by A_k gives exactly

    (m!k!/d!) (d+1)^(d+1)
      /[(m+1)^(m+1)(k+1)^k].

The same J_*(v) cancels. For m=0,k=d this is d+1. For k=1 it is the established facet coefficient divided by 2. The power parameter p=k+1 and the marginal exponent (k+1)/k are thus consistent with both the facet and vertex cases.

`supporting computation verify_retained_cap_cone_audit_defect_transport.py` independently checks the coefficients, scale derivative, cone centroid factors, all dimensions d≤16 and codimensions, actual standard-simplex vertex caps, nonsymmetric interval-face power minimizers, and both square-cone calibrations. These exact calculations supplement the analytic proof; they do not replace the cone exhaustion argument.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
